description: Turns the incremental events a host receives — from a SignalR hub, a one-second poll, an IAsyncEnumerable, a server-sent event stream — into the ONE strictly ordered tail an agent visualization may apply on top of its snapshot. The contract is a snapshot PLUS events, never a live collection: the component owns its view of the data and the host owns the transport, so this shared class is where de-duplication and hole detection live once instead of in eleven components. Ordered: Apply sorts a batch by the sequence selector, so a page merge cannot apply a block before the event that opened it. Idempotent: an event whose sequence was already applied is dropped, so the same batch genuinely arriving twice after a hub reconnect changes nothing. Contiguous: a hole is never papered over — when a sequence is missing the WHOLE batch is rejected, HasGap turns true and GapDetected is raised once with the first sequence the stream does not have, so the applied tail is always a contiguous run and the host's repair (reload the snapshot, or resend the missing range) is exact. Transport-neutral: nothing reads the clock, awaits, or knows what an event means. Thread-safe: a hub callback and a polling loop may feed the same stream; the one callback that runs OUTSIDE the gate is GapDetected, so a handler may wait for another thread to repair the stream instead of deadlocking against the applying one. A stream starts with no baseline (LastSequence is null), so the first batch may begin at 0, at 1 or at whatever number the backend restarted from; ResetToSnapshot installs the baseline of a reloaded snapshot and is also the documented repair after a gap.

members.name: LastSequence
members.description: The sequence of the last applied event, or null when nothing has been applied to a stream without a snapshot baseline yet. A host compares it with its snapshot's own sequence to decide whether the two are in sync.

members.name: HasGap
members.description: Whether the LAST Apply call found a hole. True means the host must reload the snapshot before the component can be trusted; the next batch that applies something, or ResetToSnapshot, clears it.

members.name: GapDetected
members.description: Raised once per batch that contains a hole, with the first sequence the stream does not have. Invoked synchronously on the applying thread AFTER the stream's gate is released, so a handler may call ResetToSnapshot, Apply or LastSequence — including from another thread it waits for — without deadlocking the stream. HasGap is already true when the handler starts, but the state it describes is not pinned: another feed may repair the hole while it runs.

members.name: Apply
members.description: Applies an incremental batch and returns exactly the events that are NEW, in sequence order. Nothing is returned for an already applied event, for an older one, or for any event of a batch that contains a hole, so a caller appends the returned tail to its snapshot and never de-duplicates itself.

members.name: ResetToSnapshot
members.description: Re-bases the stream on a reloaded snapshot: everything up to the supplied sequence is treated as already applied and the gap is cleared. Moving the baseline BACKWARDS is legal and is how a snapshot taken before the last events replays them.
